evals.name: quorum-never-elects-ping-works
evals.prompt: three-node automq cluster on vultr, kraft combined roles. every broker comes up and then dies about a minute later with 'Received a fatal error while waiting for the controller to acknowledge that we are caught up'. before that the log just repeats 'the loader is still catching up because we still don't know the high water mark yet' forever. i checked and all three nodes ARE listening on 9093, the controller.quorum.voters string matches the actual private ips, and i can ping every node from every other node. raft log shows each one going Candidate -> election timed out -> Candidate again, epoch is up past 50. what am i missing?
evals.expected_behaviour: Identifies that ping proves nothing about TCP and that there are two firewalls on a Vultr node: the provider group AND ufw, which the Ubuntu image ships enabled with only 22/tcp. Directs the user to test raw TCP across the private network with a listener rather than ping, and to check ufw status on the host first. Notes the broker-side fatal error is a downstream symptom, not the cause.

evals.name: scram-invalid-credentials-every-principal
evals.prompt: my automq/kafka cluster suddenly refuses every SASL login - 'Authentication failed during authentication due to invalid credentials with SASL mechanism SCRAM-SHA-512'. it's not just one user, it's the admin principal and the inter-broker one too, and i haven't changed any passwords. the secrets file is identical on all three nodes, i checked the sha256. i tried kafka-configs --bootstrap-controller to re-add the user and got UnsupportedEndpointTypeException. how do i get back in?
evals.expected_behaviour: Recognises this as a cluster formatted WITHOUT SCRAM bootstrap records, and has the user confirm it by counting USER_SCRAM_CREDENTIAL_RECORD in bootstrap.checkpoint via kafka-dump-log --cluster-metadata-decoder. Explains there is no in-place recovery and why the controller-endpoint route is closed. Gives the recovery: wipe the metadata directories, clear the format/genesis records, re-converge as a true genesis. Identifies the root cause as deciding genesis from a marker claimed before the format rather than from evidence the format completed.

evals.name: jaas-entry-missing-crashloop
evals.prompt: kafka won't start at all, restarts in a loop. the only fatal line is "Could not find a 'KafkaServer' or 'external.KafkaServer' entry in the JAAS configuration. System property 'java.security.auth.login.config' is not set". i don't want to use a jaas FILE, i'm configuring everything with listener-scoped properties, and my controller and internal listeners both have their sasl.jaas.config set and the controller endpoint even logs that it's READY. what file is it looking for?
evals.expected_behaviour: Explains that no file is missing - the public SASL_SSL/SCRAM listener needs its own listener.name.<name>.scram-sha-512.sasl.jaas.config, which carries no username or password because a SCRAM server validates against the metadata log. Notes that the controller listener reporting READY is evidence the other listeners are configured correctly, and that this one is easy to omit precisely because it looks empty.

evals.name: gate-passes-once-then-fails
evals.prompt: our deployment's smoke test produces 500 records to a topic, consumes 500 back and diffs them. it passed perfectly the first time we deployed. now every single converge fails with 'produced 500 records, consumed a different set' even though the cluster is completely healthy - brokers registered, quorum has a leader, everything. did something corrupt the topic?
evals.expected_behaviour: Identifies that nothing is wrong with the cluster: the topic persists across converges so the consumer reads the previous run's records. Explains that idempotency applies to acceptance gates too, and that a gate which only passes on a fresh cluster is a first-run demonstration. Recommends recreating the gate's topic (waiting out asynchronous deletion) or tagging records with a per-run value, and suggests auditing other gates for the same flaw.

evals.name: vpc2-not-found
evals.prompt: terraform apply against vultr fails with: Error: error creating VPC 2.0: {"error":"Not found.","status":404} on the vultr_vpc2 resource. my api key definitely works, it created the instances and the firewall group in the same apply. the resource is right there in the provider docs. is this a permissions thing on my account?
evals.expected_behaviour: Explains it is neither permissions nor a provider bug: Vultr retired the VPC 2.0 API while the provider still ships the resource and its docs. Has the user prove it with two curl calls (/v2/vpc2 returns 404, /v2/vpcs returns 200) and switch to vultr_vpc with v4_subnet/v4_subnet_mask and vpc_ids on the instance, noting internal_ip is still the private address. Draws the general lesson that provider source proves things about the client, not the endpoint.

evals.name: rf1-looks-wrong
evals.prompt: inherited an automq deployment and i think whoever set it up made a serious mistake - every topic including __consumer_offsets is replication factor 1, on a three node cluster. i want to bump everything to RF=3 before we put real traffic on it. any reason not to just do that?
evals.expected_behaviour: Explains RF=1 is the architecture, not an error: durability comes from object storage since a produce is acknowledged once the record is in the bucket, and upstream ships RF=1 defaults for the same reason. Warns that raising it adds cost and write amplification without adding durability. Distinguishes durability from availability - a partition whose leader dies is unwritable until reassignment and __consumer_offsets is RF=1 too - and recommends measuring those windows with a targeted failover test rather than changing the replication factor.

evals.name: cert-renewal-race-design
evals.prompt: designing tls for a 3 broker kafka cluster where each broker advertises its own hostname. plan was to have every node run lego with dns-01 for its own name plus the shared bootstrap name, on a systemd timer. that seems simplest - no distribution step. anything wrong with it?
evals.expected_behaviour: Flags that all three nodes issuing for the shared bootstrap name will race on the same _acme-challenge TXT record, each deleting the others' proof, and that this appears at renewal time months after the converge that created it. Also flags that it puts a zone-editing DNS credential on every publicly reachable broker. Recommends a single issuer publishing to shared storage the others pull from, and warns that restarts must be serialised by a distributed lease rather than each node's local quorum check, since combined broker+controller nodes restarting together destroy the majority.

evals.name: owned-buckets-are-not-external-adoptions
evals.prompt: The old AutoMQ context says adopt rather than create. My AWS deployment creates the backend, data and ops buckets with the SSH keypair. Should delete leave all three buckets behind to follow that rule?
evals.expected_behaviour: Distinguishes the original Vultr external R2 adoption policy from the verified AWS owned-resource lifecycle. Stops brokers before deleting application storage, destroys compute and its keypair, and finalizes the backend last including versioned state. Does not infer permission to delete data from a diagnosis request. Points to the AWS provenance and repeated-delete evidence.

evals.name: kafka-cli-inherits-broker-heap
evals.prompt: Our three AutoMQ brokers look healthy until acceptance runs kafka admin commands. Then a host reports an OOM kill. The broker heap is 2 GiB and I already allowed for that. What else should I inspect?
evals.expected_behaviour: Checks the Kafka CLI and healthcheck heap environment. Identifies the verified AWS failure where CLI processes inherited the server 2 GiB minimum heap and cites the package fix limiting those subprocesses to 256 MiB maximum. Keeps broker configuration separate and preserves serial rollout with readiness checks.

evals.name: gcs-state-key-is-workspace-object
evals.prompt: The GCS backend bucket was created, but AutoMQ bootstrap says no usable state. Our probe GETs the logical tfstate key directly using the old S3 endpoint code. Should I rerun create and let it allocate new nodes?
evals.expected_behaviour: Routes to the observed Google Cloud state-discovery trap. Checks native GCS transport and the actual default-workspace object at <logical-tfstate-key>/default.tfstate. Keeps the coordination journal at its direct key. Does not interpret a broken transport or wrong object path as evidence authorizing replacement resources.

evals.name: gcloud-bucket-missing-parser
evals.prompt: The Google compute stage already created three AutoMQ VMs. Now application bucket preflight stops on gcloud version 569.0.0 output containing lowercase not found: 404. The bucket does not appear in my project. What should I inspect before retrying?
evals.expected_behaviour: Identifies the observed absence-parser mismatch and checks the exact provider response. Treats the specific missing-bucket response as absence while preserving fail-closed behavior for auth errors and other failures. Explains compute success does not prove application storage was created, and retains live state during retry.

evals.name: google-security-archive-timeout
evals.prompt: AutoMQ on Google Cloud created its machines and buckets, but the base apt task has been stuck for several minutes. From one node security.ubuntu.com times out, while the us-central1.gce.archive.ubuntu.com noble-security InRelease returns 200. Can I remove the apt lock and retry?
evals.expected_behaviour: Diagnoses the observed security archive reachability issue, points to the optional automq-apt-security-mirror setting, and preserves Suites, Components and Signed-By. Checks whether remote apt workers remain active after stopping Ansible and waits for locks to become free naturally. Does not remove package-manager lock files or treat bucket creation as proof of Kafka acceptance.

evals.name: gcs-conditional-header-dialect
evals.prompt: My boto3 GCS request with x-goog-if-generation-match got ExcessHeaderValues: Requests cannot specify both x-amz and x-goog headers. I renamed it x-amz-if-generation-match and now both writers get 200. Is conditional ownership working?
evals.expected_behaviour: Recognizes mixed signing/header dialects and the verified silently ignored x-amz condition alias. Requires coherent x-goog headers before canonical signing and negative live tests: competitor create and stale generation replacement must fail while initial create and exact-generation replacement succeed. Does not treat HTTP 200 as proof of conditional semantics or isolated signing probes as full deployment acceptance.

evals.name: oci-stale-etag-write-succeeds
evals.prompt: My OCI S3 compatibility probe rejects a second If-None-Match create with 412. A PUT with the current ETag succeeds, but another PUT with that old ETag also returns 200 and the GET says stale. Can I trust this endpoint for expired AutoMQ restart lease takeover?
evals.expected_behaviour: Routes to the verified OCI compatibility failure. Explains that conditional creation and conditional replacement are separate contracts and the stale PUT violated replacement exclusion. Requires a native conditional operation or another proven compare-and-swap path, negative stale-writer tests and final-value checks through the installed client. Does not accept the successful create condition as proof of lease safety or claim full cluster acceptance from a storage probe.

evals.name: oci-customer-secret-propagation
evals.prompt: I just created an OCI customer secret key for AutoMQ. The compatibility endpoint still refuses authentication several minutes later. Should I generate another secret, or just sleep for eight minutes?
evals.expected_behaviour: Uses the observed OCI propagation interval without treating it as a provider guarantee. Reports the last failed sample at 7 minutes 15.456 seconds and first success at 8 minutes 15.498 seconds after creation. Retains the generated secret, uses bounded authenticated readiness probes, separates credential readiness from bucket permissions, and never prints the secret.

evals.name: oci-state-404-isolation
evals.prompt: The AutoMQ application key gets 404 when it reads the OCI state bucket. I want to mark backend isolation passed. The same bucket might also be missing. What proves which explanation is right?
evals.expected_behaviour: Requires operator-identity native bucket and ownership-object existence checks before interpreting application 403 or concealed 404 as denial. Uses the same existing resource for the application probe and refuses to equate 404 alone with either safe isolation or absence.

evals.name: oci-zero-memory-ratio-and-capacity
evals.prompt: OCI refuses my AutoMQ A2 launch with Invalid ratio of memory in GB to OCPUs. Current ratio: 4.0. Valid ratio range: 0 - 0. I requested 1 OCPU and 8GB, the shape says flexible and my limits are positive. A1 in the same region says Out of host capacity. Should I set memory to zero or assume the provider doubled my OCPUs?
evals.expected_behaviour: Routes to the observed OCI provisioning failures. Does not interpret zero-range metadata as a valid zero-memory configuration or invent a quota cause. Distinguishes A2 core/OCPU accounting from requested OCPUs and notes that 8GiB, 6GiB and omitted-memory attempts all failed. Checks image compatibility, shape metadata, limits and actual allocation independently. Explains positive limits do not establish physical capacity and does not claim cluster acceptance when no VM launched.

evals.name: oci-service-user-primary-email
evals.prompt: My AutoMQ OCI storage stage created buckets, then oci_identity_user.application failed with IdcsConversionError: The primary email must be specified. The provider let me omit email. Should I delete the state and rerun?
evals.expected_behaviour: Identifies the observed Identity Domains requirement. Sets explicit tenancy-unique automq-oci-user-email, preserves existing stage state, and distinguishes a failed user operation from rollback of buckets and other resources. Does not claim successful broker acceptance from a completed storage stage.

evals.name: oci-failed-create-needs-absence-proof
evals.prompt: OCI rejected all AutoMQ VM launches. I changed A2 to A1, but compute still refuses the failed create. The node state has serial1 and no params. Can I clear the failed operation in the journal?
evals.expected_behaviour: Uses the pinned compute library explicit OCI recovery function instead of manual journal edits. Requires current failed operation IDs, empty valid state and complete native VM/boot-volume absence checks under the journal lease, across the original compartment and domains. Treats terminating resources and empty CLI stdout as insufficient absence evidence. Notes resource-name matching limits after out-of-band renames.

evals.name: oci-partial-delete-skips-owned-resources
evals.prompt: No AutoMQ VM ever launched on OCI, but I have three owned buckets, an NSG and application IAM keys. After recovering the failed creates, delete jumps straight to backend finalization, which refuses active state. Does no running VM mean I can bypass that check and delete the backend?
evals.expected_behaviour: Identifies the partial-deployment deletion routing defect. Distinguishes inspection error from verified absence, keeps finalizer refusal intact, and requires owned application storage/IAM, shared resources and SSH key cleanup before state finalization. Explains that declared never-created nodes with validated empty state need a journal/state transition rather than provider destruction. Does not infer a successful cleanup from the absence of VMs or a safe refusal.

evals.name: oci-bucket-update-wrong-method
evals.prompt: My AutoMQ state bucket marker says deleting and the journal is retired, but native PUT on the bucket endpoint gets 404 NotFound during finalization. No versions have been purged yet. Should I assume the bucket vanished and remove its local state?
evals.expected_behaviour: Identifies the verified UpdateBucket method mismatch: native OCI bucket updates use POST. Checks operation and method before interpreting 404 as absence. Preserves deleting marker and retired journal, resumes normal finalization after the method correction, and does not create a replacement backend or bypass ownership guards.

evals.name: oci-retired-held-journal-resume
evals.prompt: The AutoMQ compute journal is retired, its identity is right, and backend finalization was interrupted while holding its lease. Normal delete now says compute state unavailable; legacy monolithic state requires explicit migration. Is this actually old state that I need to migrate?
evals.expected_behaviour: Identifies the verified classification-order defect. Requires valid journal schema and matching deployment identity before recognizing retired status, then routes to guarded backend finalization even if its old finalizer lease is held. Keeps active held journals excluded, and does not infer legacy state from the generic error or manually clear ownership evidence.
